Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Main Title (1:03)  "This is a piece that symbolizes the Ogre series. We layered instruments to add texture while still remaining faithful to the original orchestration." (Kudo)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Kimihiro Abe  Introduction (2:59)  "Iwata handled the chorus, while I added texture to the orchestration. The result was even more lavish than we expected, and I feel it really draws players into the story." (Abe)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battle Party Formation (0:46)  "Warriors experience all manner of emotions as they prepare for battle. This piece aims to express these feelings." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Victory Screen (0:48)  "I aimed to recreate the joy and relief of victory, and, in the new parts, the excitement of collecting the spoils of war." (Iwata)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Retreat (0:30)  "This piece represents the sounds of soldiers fleeing from battle." (Iwata)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Game Over (0:17)  "I aimed to reflect the sadness and regret of death and defeat." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  World Map (1:26)  "The game revolves around epic battles, so we used a more relaxed piece for the map screen. We extended the piece slightly, aiming for the feeling of reaching your destination at sunset after a long journey." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 3 (2:00)  "Nybeth commands the dead, meddling with souls in his quest for immortality. This can be thought of as his theme. A rhythm that portrays a resonating darkness has been added to the eerie scale of the original." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 5 (3:12)  "We added an ominously escalating flourish to the end of the original. I think the interplay between organ and orchestra is particularly poignant." (Kudo)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 7 (2:29)  "Battles must be fought to the bitter end. This mentality and the chaos of battle are portrayed in a piece slightly longer than the original." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 9 (1:47)  "We took care not to interfere with the atmosphere of the original. I think we captured the essence of Denam's will to battle on valiantly." (Kamikura)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 11 (1:25)  "I gave this piece the sense of a battle that sees feats both daring and measured." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Final Battle (3:10)  "This is a battle against a foe not of this world. I touched upon the fear, mistrust, and brutality such a battle brings." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Kimihiro Abe  Challenge Battles (1:10)  "We kept the melody and chordal progression of the original while giving it a broader sound and adding trills to make this a piece suitable even for live performance." (Abe)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 1 (2:40)  "This is one of a few pieces that use a rhythm section with drums. We used trial and error to match it to the scene it is first played, adopting a composition that conveys impotent rage and hopelessness." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Character Creation (1:01)  "This is the first piece I worked on. The aim was to faithfully reproduce the notes of the original. Working to a simple plan like this isn't as easy as it may seem." (Kaneda)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Data Selection Screen (1:19)  "The chorus felt muted in the first half, and we rebalanced it several times. The second half is a smooth composition using harpsichord and strings." (Kaneda)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Azusa Chiba  Battlefield 4 (2:20)  "The original was an energetic piece containing many harmonic cadences, so we used a dramatic arrangement for the second half based on the original. I think the tubular bells in this section create good tension." (Chiba)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 8 (1:26)  "We struggled to find the right tone for the rhythm instruments. In the end we added an orchestral touch to the drum machine tone used in the original, resulting in the final piece." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 12 (2:51)  "The intense and dramatic shifts in this piece match the weight of responsibility in the scene perfectly. We added a new part to the end of the original, using harps and other tones to render sounds reminiscent of the open sky." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 13 (2:39)  "We added new touches to the intro and end of the original piece. This is an extremely dense piece with elaborately interwoven textures, and we put considerable effort into living up to the standards set." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Chapter Title (1:09)  "As the overarching story of the game is serious in tone, we added new touches with a melancholic atmosphere to the middle section, aiming to cast a little shadow on the piece." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Warren Report (1:24)  "We wanted a calmer piece that gave players a break from the hectic pace, so we focused on stringed instruments such as the cello to create a gentle, ephemeral tone." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Hitoshi Sakimoto  End Titles (5:57)  "I often have mixed emotions when I listen to one of my older pieces. I can still clearly remember all the points I dwelled upon at the time." (Sakimoto)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 6 (1:05)  "This is not an intense piece, but it is affecting in its own way, perhaps through the chilling sadness or hardships of battle it conveys." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 10 (2:03)  "This piece imparts a sense of courageousness and tension while hammering home the brutality of battle. We added new phrasing and melody to the end of the original." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Prologue (1:29)  "This piece contains dramatic transitions, with the Dark Knights' theme inserted into the middle. It is a memorable piece, fitting for a scene of Lanselot Tartaros standing at the clifftops." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Battlefield 2 (2:07)  "A simple piece using strings and brass that maintains a persistent rhythm, with bold transitions towards the second half having a recurring theme." (Kaneda)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Music Box 1 (not used) (0:24)  "The song played by Lanselot's keepsake music box. The sorrowful refrain calls to mind tragedies both past and still to come." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Music Box 2 (not used) (1:13)  "This piece captures the rush of emotions when learning of a tragedy. It is a song for those at the mercy of time, unable to unwind the clock. For the remake we added music box sounds that convey a sense of unbearable loss." (Iwata)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Azusa Chiba  Walister Resistance Theme (0:25)  "The single timbre used for the strings lacked boldness, so we layered on different tones. The result is a crisp, bold staccato." (Chiba)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Secret Talks (0:47)  "This piece was created to represent negotiations held in secret. It conveys the sense of mischief inherent in discussions held behind closed doors." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  The Bakram Theme (1:25)  "This piece evokes dealings with the privileged classes and nobility. I worked hard to elicit an atmosphere not found in everyday conversations." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  The Loslorien Theme (0:55)  "This piece suggests a procession marching on into the fading twilight, then coming silently to a halt. This is what I aimed to recreate." (Iwata)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Crisis (0:27)  "The piece evokes something moving stealthily in the darkness, but as it is often played before battle we took care to preserve the brass staccato to retain its brisk feeling." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Conversations (1:54)  "We aimed for the feeling of hymns reverberating throughout a cathedral, placing emphasis on the timbre of the chorus, and adding a celestial melody to the new portions." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Denam's Theme (1:39)  "This piece abounds with the sense of valor and the exuberance of youth. We have extended the original, and hinted at the trouble that is to befall him with a melody using stringed instruments." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Azusa Chiba  Catiua's Theme (0:43)  "We wanted to strike a good balance between soft and sharp tones, and tried a number of different harps until we found the right one. The tempo is slower than the original, and we have tweaked the variations." (Chiba)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Shock (0:44)  "The piece is designed to convey the sense of an undesirable truth being revealed. I gave it an exaggerated tone." (Iwata)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Somber Atmosphere 1 (0:33)  "We attempted to express a somber scene with slight elements of fear." (Iwata)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Azusa Chiba  Somber Atmosphere 2 (1:49)  "The latter half is a new addition. Making use of the bleak but tense instrument composition of the first half of the original, we added a hint of sorrow to the melody." (Chiba)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Somber Atmosphere 3 (1:20)  "We wanted to include elements of a requiem for the dead, and so incorporated dramatic transitions that bestow a feeling of solemnity and grief." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Epilogue 1 (1:15)  "This piece conveys a great sense of loss. As with the ending, I remember it leaving a lasting impression on me when I played the original game." (Kudo)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Epilogue 2 (0:49)  "This piece also faithfully recreates the notes of the original, with the sound sources replaced to convey a feeling of floating above a sea of clouds." (Kaneda)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Epilogue 3 (0:29)  "This piece has a fanfare-like quality, and I recall taking care not to make it overly showy or gaudy, taking into account my mental picture of each character appearing on the screen." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 14 (1:06)  "I'm sure this brings back memories for many players. It is truly a piece that evokes the Ogre Battle series! We again sought to flesh it out by polishing the orchestral sounds of the original." (Kudo)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 15 (1:06)  "This is the piece I struggled with most on this title. Through trial and error it settled into an invigorating melody that evokes a voyage across the great deep, and I think it has come out well." (Kamikura)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Battlefield 16 (1:07)  "This piece uses a large number of voices, which makes it difficult to avoid clouding the nuance of each tone. It was challenging to instill the emotions we were aiming for." (Kaneda)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 17 (1:07)  "We changed the rhythm instruments from the original, but made as much use of the wonderful melody and ethereal chords as we could." (Kudo)

Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 18 (1:18)  "This piece presents a wide range of tempos and emotions. We drew upon the inherent flavor of the original while working on it. I hope that players enjoy the changes in emotion during the song while they play the game." (Kamikura)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Mitsuhiro Kaneda  Battlefield 19 (1:16)  "For this piece we focused on intimidating sounds, such as the timpani, that convey the sense of a large force descending upon you at speed. We had a hard time getting the chorus for this piece to stand out." (Kaneda)

Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 20 (1:10)  "This piece maintains consistent vigor from the intro through to the end. By adding woodwind instruments and percussion instruments such as the xylophone, I believe we have expressed vigor and further momentum." (Kamikura)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  New Music Box 1 (0:23)  "The new music box piece is a typical song that could be found in any music box." (Iwata)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  New Music Box 2 (1:16)  "I arranged this new music box piece to convey overwhelming feelings of loss and despondency." (Iwata)
Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Hitoshi Sakimoto  Battlefield 21 (1:51)  "I wrote this new piece to have a slightly different disposition." (Sakimoto)
Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Hitoshi Sakimoto  Battlefield 22 (1:36)  "I incorporated techniques not available at the time to make this new piece slightly more warlike." (Sakimoto)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 23 (2:11)  "This piece captures the essence of fighting your way through to victory as the battle continues to escalate." (Iwata)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Hitoshi Sakimoto  Battlefield 24 (2:05)  "The first part conveys unease while the second is more frantic, so I began with the theme of the Dark Knights, and used the Ogre Battle theme later in the piece." (Sakimoto)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 25 (2:58)  "This piece is my interpretation of a final battle between bitter enemies." (Iwata)
Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  The Holy Knight Lanselot's Theme (1:57)  "This piece is unique among songs of the Ogre series. I aimed to convey warmth when writing it." (Iwata)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Kimihiro Abe  Somber Atmosphere 4 (2:21)  "We used the ideas behind the original to create a new piece. The delivery of this idea using woodwind instruments is one of the listening points here." (Abe)

Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Somber Atmosphere 5 (1:26)  "We set out to use woodwind instruments in contrast with the seriousness of the original to give it slightly less severity." (Kudo)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  New Music Box 3 (0:30)  "This piece conveys a broken music box. The music stops abruptly at the end as if the box had expended all its energy. It was a challenge to express the broken nature of the box, and the first attempt was a little heavy handed, so we recreated it with a more subtle tone." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Iuria's Song (0:33)  "For Iuria's song we wanted to create a song that a person free of all constraints would sing. This is how I see the winged folk." (Iwata)

Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  New Music Box 4 (1:34)  "Using the melody of the music box that appears during the story, we switched over the harmony to create a piece that conveys hopelessness and a sense of loss." (Kudo)

A Walister hailing from Golyat. His father, Prancet, was taken away by the Dark Knights when they attacked Golyat a year earlier. {hero} rallied to the cause of the Walister Resistance, harrying Bakram and Galgastani forces together with sister Catiua and friend Vyce.

A Walister hailing from Golyat. His father, Prancet, was taken away by the Dark Knights when they attacked Golyat a year earlier. {hero} rallied to the cause of the Walister Resistance, harrying the enemies of his people together with sister Catiua and friend Vyce.
  Aided by a band of Xenobians he met in Golyat, he freed Walister leader Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle. He was then offered a place in the Walister Resistance, becoming captain of the Order of {order}.
  Called the Hero of Golyat by his people, he soon became a prominent figure in the Resistance.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Walister Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle. He later broke his ties with them after opposing the duke's plan to unite the people by slaughtering Walister at Balmamusa. He is currently in hiding with his sister Catiua, awaiting an opportunity to overthrow the Duke.

A member of the Walister Resistance hailing from Golyat. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle. Together with Sir Leonar he took part in the killing of Walister civilians at Balmamusa, hoping to unite his people against the enemy. For his loyalty he was made a senior officer of the Resistance.
  The enemy call him the "Butcher of Golyat," and he is hunted by those who know the truth behind the massacre at Balmamusa.

A member of the Walister Resistance hailing from Golyat. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, but left for a time due to their involvement in the massacre at Balmamusa.
  He went into hiding with sister Catiua, but eventually rejoined the Resistance when Sir Leonar appealed to him for aid following the Bakram invasion of Rhime. He now continues to battle the Bakram, seeking to drive them from Walister lands.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle. Due to the massacre at Balmamusa he broke his ties with the Resistance and went into hiding with Catiua.
  In battle with Sir Leonar he learned the Duke planned to forge a secret treaty with the Dark Knights Loslorien. He set off for Rhime to stop the proceedings, but before he could act the duke was killed through Vyce's treachery. With the Resistance rudderless he offered to take the helm, and he now commands all of southern Valeria.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, and later took part in the massacre at Balmamusa.
  Upon ousting Sir Leonar, who had slain the Duke over doubts about his fitness to lead, he took control of the Resistance. He also made peace with Vyce's New Walister Alliance, demonstrating a caliber of leadership beyond his years.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, and later took part in the massacre at Balmamusa. Despite setbacks he eventually came to lead the Resistance against the Bakram and Dark Knight forces.
  His people call him the "Hero of Golyat," and have faith that he can put an end to the ravages of war.

A Bakram hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, and later took part in the massacre at Balmamusa. Despite setbacks he eventually came to lead the Resistance against the Bakram and Dark Knight forces.
  He was reunited with his father, Prancet, at Brigantys Castle, and from him learned the truth of Catiua's past. Olivya also revealed he was actually born in Heim of Bakram descent, with his father the brother of Regent Brantyn Morne. He now seeks to destroy the Dark Knights to fulfill his father's dying wish.

A Bakram hailing from Golyat who leads the Order of {order}. He joined the Resistance after freeing Duke Ronwey from his imprisonment at Almorica Castle, and later took part in the massacre at Balmamusa. Despite setbacks he eventually came to lead the Resistance against the Bakram and Dark Knight forces.
  He was reunited with his father, Prancet, at Brigantys Castle, and from him learned the truth of Catiua's past. Olivya also revealed he was actually born in Heim of Bakram descent, with his father the brother of Regent Brantyn Morne. He fulfilled his father's dying wish and led the Resistance to victory against the Dark Knights, defeating them in a bloody battle.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. His father was slain a year ago when the Dark Knights Loslorien attacked Golyat. With his mother already dead, he was left an orphan.
  He came to deeply resent the Bakram and Galgastani for their oppression of the Walister, and resolved to fight for his people's freedom.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. He was formerly the leader of the New Walister Alliance.
  Together with {hero} he rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance. He later broke his ties with the Resistance after strongly opposing the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa. He went on to form the New Walister Alliance to champion Walister self-rule and break the nobility's grip on power, earning much favor from his people.
  He eventually reconciled with the Resistance when {hero} took up its leadership. His might in arms served the Order of {order} well, helping bring the war to an end.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance. He took part in the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa despite {hero}'s opposition, creating a rift between them.
  The Duke rewarded his loyalty by appointing him the leader of the Resistance's Third Spear.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance. He took part in the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa despite {hero}'s opposition, creating a rift between them.
  The Duke rewarded his loyalty by appointing him the leader of the Resistance's Third Spear. He was ordered to do away with those who know the truth of Balmamusa, and he now seeks to kill {hero}.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance.
  He later broke his ties with the Resistance after strongly opposing the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa. His whereabouts are currently unknown.

He went on to form the New Walister Alliance to champion Walister self-rule and break the nobility's grip on power, earning much favor from his people.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He took part in the massacre at Balmamusa and was made leader of the Duke's personal guard. However, unable to come to terms with {hero}'s reinstatement into the Resistance, he took flight.
  Falsely accused by the Resistance of plotting to kill Duke Ronwey, a hefty bounty of 50,000 goth has been placed on his head.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He took part in the massacre at Balmamusa and was made leader of the Duke's personal guard. However, unable to come to terms with {hero}'s reinstatement into the Resistance, he took flight.
  With an unprecedented sum of 60,000 goth on his head, he is pursued by the Resistance and headhunters alike.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He took part in the massacre at Balmamusa and was made leader of the Duke's personal guard. However, unable to come to terms with {hero}'s reinstatement into the Resistance, he took flight.
  Realizing he had been used, he stole in and slew the Duke while Resistance forces were engaged in the retaking of Rhime. He then met his end at the hands of Resistance soldiers.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He later took part in the massacre of Walister at Balmamusa despite {hero}'s opposition, creating a rift between them. His loyalty to the Resistance was rewarded through his promotion to leader of a force reporting directly to the Duke.
  However, his lust for power led him to conspire with the Bakram and slay the Duke. He also plotted to kill the Dark Knight Lanselot, but failed in his attempt. The Bakram laid sole blame on him, and he was executed for his crime.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. He was formerly the leader of the New Walister Alliance.

He went on to form the New Walister Alliance to champion Walister self-rule and break the nobility's grip on power, earning much favor from his people.
  He eventually reconciled with the Resistance when {hero} took up its leadership. His might in arms serves the Order of {order} well as they strive to put an end to the war.

A Walister hailing from Golyat who grew up with {hero}. Together they rescued Duke Ronwey and joined the Walister Resistance, where he once commanded the Third Spear.
  He later took part in the massacre of innocent Walister at Balmamusa despite {hero}'s opposition, creating a rift between them. He continued to serve the Resistance thereafter, commanding a force reporting directly to the Duke. However, his lust for power led him to conspire with the Bakram and make an attempt on the lives of the Duke and the Dark Knight Lanselot. He was hanged by the Bakram after the plot failed.
  Following his death he was reanimated by the Necromancer Nybeth, but then defeated by {hero}, finally putting his tormented soul to rest.

A Walister hailing from Golyat. She is sister to {hero}. After the Dark Knights attacked her hometown of Golyat, she joined {hero} and Vyce in striking back at their oppressors.
  As Catiua's mother died when she was young, she assumed the maternal role in the family. Her father, Prancet, has trained her in the ways of the sibyl.

Catiua's true name is Versalia Oberyth. She is sister to {hero}. After the Dark Knights attacked her hometown of Golyat, she joined {hero} in striking back at their oppressors.
  She went into hiding after opposing the massacre at Balmamusa, but returned to the Resistance fold after the Bakram invasion of Rhime.
  Believing {hero} to be her only true kin, she became distraught at the distance that had grown between them, and decided to leave the Resistance. Upon her return to Golyat, the Dark Knight Lanselot informed her she was the daughter of the Dynast-King and the Queen's handmaiden Mannaflora. Her current whereabouts are not known.

Catiua's true name is Versalia Oberyth. She is sister to {hero}. After the Dark Knights attacked her hometown of Golyat, she joined {hero} in striking back at their oppressors. She went into hiding after opposing the massacre at Balmamusa, but returned to the Resistance fold after the Bakram invasion of Rhime.
  Believing {hero} to be her only true kin, she became distraught at the distance that had grown between them, and decided to leave the Resistance. Upon her return to Golyat, the Dark Knight Lanselot informed her she was the daughter of the Dynast-King and the Queen's handmaiden Mannaflora.

  House Grandier traces its lineage back to Lord Clemont of Barnicia, and many have held official posts over the generations. They also served as knights to King Dorgalua, and now hold sway in both military and civil matters.
  Latimer had frequented Heim Castle as a squire since his youth, seeking to hone his skills and become an exemplary knight. He was an accomplished man-at-arms and commander, well-liked by both his men and the people of Heim for his gallantry.
  These qualities led to him being charged with the defense of Heim Castle. He was killed fighting the Order of {order}.

A guardian of the Palace of the Dead. The statues lining the halls of the palace are actually unlucky explorers turned to stone by her magic.
  Xadoba was hideously disfigured in her true form, but was said to appear as a beautiful maiden before visitors to the palace. Those who inhabit the realm of chaos are adept at manipulating mortal minds, and can bend them to their will with ease.
  Xadoba was defeated by {hero} after attempting to prevent his passage through the palace.

A Galgastani who led a band of pirates that plagued the Obero Sea. He was born in one of the poorer quarters of Port Asyton, and spent his youth serving in a local tavern. There he became acquainted with the notorious pirate Lontera, and later joined his crew. When Lontera was executed by the Valerian army, Darza took the helm in his stead.
  His wife Veldrei was born to nobility, but became a pirate after Darza raided the vessel on which she had taken passage near Boed Fortress. Veldrei stayed ashore to watch over their den at Ndamsa Fortress after learning she carried Darza's child.
  Darza attacked members of the Liberation Front at Qadriga Fortress, commandeering their ship and cargo. However, before he could escape he was killed by Sir Folcurt and {hero}, who had arrived to free the hostages.

A Galgastani who led a band of pirates that plagued the Obero Sea. He was born in one of the poorer quarters of Port Asyton, and spent his youth serving in a local tavern. There he became acquainted with the notorious pirate Lontera, and later joined his crew. When Lontera was executed by the Valerian army, Darza took the helm in his stead.
  He met Resistance forces while en route to Qadriga Fortress in pursuit of Xapan, and was killed by {hero}.

A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. Sir Hektor was among the Galgastani taken prisoner after Coritanae Keep fell to the Resistance. He was pressed for information regarding remaining Balbatos loyalists, but steadfastly refused to speak. He was eventually slain at Almorica Castle.

A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. He was a knight of House Didarro, a family of note in Coritanae. They have served the Lord of Coritanae for many generations, and are fiercely loyal to the Kingdom of Galgastan. Hektor was to wed Moldova until she fell in battle at Krysaro.
  He was garrisoned at Brigantys Castle under High Commander Xaebos, but later set off for the Bahanna Highlands to aid Moldova's sister, Cressida. He escorted Cressida to Brigantys Castle safely, but was then killed by the Order of {order}.

A Galgastani who serves his clan in battle. He is a knight of House Didarro, a family of note in Coritanae. They have served the Lord of Coritanae for many generations, and are fiercely loyal to the Kingdom of Galgastan. He was garrisoned at Brigantys Castle under High Commander Xaebos.
  He later encountered the Resistance while patrolling the Madura Drift. A battle ensued, but Hektor withdrew to Brigantys Castle after seeing he was outmatched.

Hektor kept reports of the Resistance's advance from reaching Coritanae, and laid down his life, allowing the Resistance to take Brigantys Castle.

A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. At the start of the war he led a group of bandits based in the Phorampa Wildwood, but a desire to defend his homeland prompted him to enlist as a man-at-arms.

In an attempt to prove himself he led an offensive against partisans at Almorica Castle. However, his poor reputation was only compounded when he was slain by those he sought to bring to justice. He met his end at the hands of {hero}, the Hero of Golyat himself.

A Bakram who belonged to a special detachment sent to the Palace of the Dead at Regent Morne's behest to search for draconic magic. Born to a family of poisoners, she was well versed in the use of toxins and venoms. Her detachment included many such sages and masters of arcane lore, their task being the recovery of rare and legendary artifacts. She was killed in a clash with Resistance forces below the palace.

A Galgastani who served his clan in battle. During the reign of King Dorgalua, deadly swordfights were a popular form of entertainment among wealthy Bakram in Heim. Only gladiators were permitted to participate in these bouts to the death. These gladiators were deserters or criminals chosen for their fighting ability. By choosing the path of the gladiator they escaped execution and were granted a small chance of freedom.
  Brezen was once a gladiator himself, surviving numerous bouts to eventually win his liberty. His skill in battle saw him recruited into the army, but he was disliked by others for his vulgar manners. He was bullied mercilessly and made the target of much unjustified scorn. Perhaps because of this, his prowess on the field of battle waned.
  He was killed after clashing with {hero} Pavel on the Golborza Plain.

An enigmatic young woman. She was seen using an artifact of some kind at the Palace of the Dead, but her identity remains a mystery. She does not seem to be affiliated with any particular faction. She appears to have an understanding of the power that flows throughout the Palace of the Dead.

An enigmatic young woman. Little is known of her except that she was not human, having taken possession of the body she inhabited. She is thought to have been a guardian of Ashmedai's palace―the Palace of the Dead―as she was conversant with the forces of chaos, and liches and other undead did her bidding.
  She was slain after a number of clashes with Resistance forces. However, if her final words are to be believed, her soul will live on beyond the loss of her corporeal form.

A Galgastani who serves her clan in battle. She was apprenticed to the Necromancer Nybeth. By studying death in all its forms, she believed it would one day be possible to cheat death entirely.
  When Nybeth set out for Qadriga Fortress to conduct his experiments, she was ordered to stay behind in Krysaro.   She was betrothed to Hektor, head of House Didarro of Coritanae, and their wedding was close at hand. She was killed in a battle against the Walister Resistance at Krysaro.

A Walister who once served with the Walister Resistance. She was a spiritualist at the village of Vanan near the border of Almorica, contacting the dead to pass on messages to their kin. Regardless of whether her talents were genuine, Ramidos brought peace to many grieving loved ones. Her father died at an early age, and it is clear that her mother instilled in her a strong sense of compassion.
  She lived in Vanan with her son's family, but all her kin were slain when the village was sacked in the early days of the war. She then joined the Walister Resistance as a spellbinder, specializing in offensive magic.
  She was killed in battle when {hero} arrived at Almorica Castle to free Catiua, who had been kidnapped by Xapan the Mercenary.

For generations they have held seats in the House of Nobles, wielding great power throughout the region. Press the {icon 12} button while viewing the world map or during battle to display the System Menu.
  Select the Data command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Options command to change settings such as the controls. In some cases the Retreat or Withdraw commands may also be available. Select these commands when you want to end the battle and return to the world map.

Use the Save command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Load command to resume a saved game. You can save or load from the world map at any time by selecting the Data command from the System Menu.

- Quick Saves -
  Select Return to Title (Quick Save) to save your game during battle. This will suspend the battle so you can resume it at a later time. To resume your game, select Single Player and then Continue on the title screen. Note that quick saves are not erased after being loaded.

A help message appears at the top of the screen for items selected by the cursor. To view help messages for items that cannot be selected, press the {icon 11} button. These select help messages can be useful when there is a large amount of information on screen, such as when viewing the party screen.

The game records your last 50 actions during battle. You can use the Chariot Tarot to call up this battle record and return to a previous point in a fight. When jumping to a previous point it is saved as a separate record, so you can compare results from before and after you retraced your steps.

- Using the Chariot Tarot -
  Press the {icon 9} button during the attack turn of one of your units or after interrupting the turns of others. You can also select Chariot Tarot from the System Menu.

- Same Actions, Same Results -
  If you perform the same actions after retracing your steps using the Chariot Tarot, the results will also be the same. You must perform different actions to change your fate in battle.

- Battle Log -
  Press the {icon 4} button while the Chariot Tarot is displayed to view a detailed log of each turn.

You can use the World Tarot to jump to certain points in previously completed areas of the story. These are called "anchor points."

- Moving Between Anchor Points -
  There are multiple anchor points in each chapter. You can view these by using the World Tarot command in the Warren Report. This time line is also used to select a specific anchor point to jump to.

- The Story is Reset -
  Your progress is saved as you pass each anchor point. When you jump to an anchor point, you resume playing from that point in the story. If you return to a point before an important decision is made, you can make that decision again.

- Your Party Remains Unchanged -
  Party details such as class levels, inventory, and war funds are retained when you jump to an anchor point. This is also true of units added to your party, though they may revert to guests not under your control depending on story developments. Even in these cases, they will always return to your party once their duties are complete.

- Lost Information -
  Each anchor point records your progress up to the point at which you passed it. For this reason, anything occurring after the selected anchor point will be lost.

Each anchor point records your progress up to the point you passed it. The status of each unit relating to the story is also saved. This means that when you use the World Tarot, you may experience some inconsistencies.

  For example, assume you had dismissed Canopus before passing Anchor Point B. If you later jump to Anchor Point B using the World Tarot, even if Canopus happens to be in your party, the story will continue on as if he had been dismissed. The same is true of the information in the Warren Report.

- Updating Anchor Point Data -
  Each time you pass an anchor point the data it contains is updated. Using the example above, if you jump to an anchor point before Canopus was dismissed, then pass Anchor Point B again without dismissing him, the Anchor Point B data will be updated to reflect his presence in your party.

You can move between various locations and customize your party on the world map.

- Main Menu -
  Press the {icon 3} button while the cursor is on your party to display the Main Menu for the world map. The Party and Warren Report commands can be used at any point on the map, while the Shop command only appears when your party is at a town or castle.

- Traversing the Map -
  To move to locations such as towns and castles, position the cursor over the desired destination and press the {icon 3} button. Events or battles may be triggered when you arrive at or pass through a map location.

- System Menu -
  Press the {icon 12} button to display the System Menu. Select the Data command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Options command to change settings such as the controls.

Some locations, such as castles, are comprised of multiple areas in which you may face several battles in a row. However, you can save your progress between battles. As on the world map, you can use Data on the System Menu to save.

- Saving Your Progress -
  You will not be able to leave a location until you have fought your way through the final stage. The use of multiple save games is strongly recommended.

Before going into battle you must select the units to send into the fray. The units that take part in a battle are called the battle party. You can deploy up to 12 units in your battle party, but this number may be reduced on some battlefields.

- Terms of Victory -
  You can view the factors that will determine victory or defeat by selecting Terms of Victory. This information can be valuable when putting together your forces.

- Unit List -
  As with the Party command on the world map, you can use the Unit List command to change the equipment or skills of your units and examine the party's inventory.

When battle starts, the unit with the lowest RT (Recovery Time) acts first. AT (Attack Turn) indicates the order that units take action.

- Attack Turn -
  You can issue commands such as Move and Act on a unit's attack turn. To issue a command, select a unit and press the {icon 3} button. Main Menu commands such as Move and Act will be displayed on the screen.

- Interrupt -
  You cannot issue commands during the attack turns of units not under your control. Press the {icon 4} button if you wish to confirm the status of units at times such as this. This interrupts the current unit's attack turn and allows you to use commands.

Units can use the Move, Act, and Skills commands once each per attack turn. There is no restriction on the order in which these commands must be used. Skills can affect Move and Act commands, so a number of tactical options are available.
  Move commands can be reset and issued again up until the point another command is issued. This can be useful when you need to reposition a unit to be in range to attack.

During battle the RT (Recovery Time) of units is compared to determine attack turn order, with units having lower RT taking their turn sooner. RT is determined by the base value for the unit, the weight of the equipment they carry, their class, and the actions they performed on their previous attack turn.

- Equipment Weight -
  Each piece of equipment displays a value for its weight. The greater its weight, the more it adds to the RT of units equipping it. It pays to take this into account when deciding which equipment to use.

- Class -
  Each class has a base RT value. The RT of similar units will vary depending on their class, affecting the order in which they act.

- Previous Attack Turn -
  Each action that is taken during an attack turn will have an impact on the RT for the next turn. This is determined by the distance covered with the Move command and the actions taken with Act and Skills commands. Equipment and spells also have RT values that are added to RT when they are used.

- Attack Turn List -
  When a unit is selected during battle, the row of units shown at the bottom of the screen indicates the expected AT order. To view the attack turn of all units in battle, press the {icon 4} button to display the Unit List, and use Sort Units to display them in order of attack turn.

  It is crucial to stay aware of which units will be acting next. Try to eliminate unnecessary actions to stay ahead of the enemy.

Select Return to Title (Quick Save) to save your game during battle. This will suspend the battle so you can resume it at a later time. To resume your game, select Single Player and then Continue on the title screen. Note that quick saves are not erased after being loaded.

Each unit has Life and HP that represent their physical endurance. Units whose HP falls to 0 during battle are incapacitated, and will lose a point of life if not aided. When a unit's life is exhausted, it is dead and can no longer be revived.

- Incapacitation -
  A counter appears above the heads of units incapacitated when their HP falls to 0. Each attack turn the counter decreases by 1, and if it reaches 0 that unit loses a life and is withdrawn from the battlefield.

- Withdrawn Units -
  Units withdrawn from the battlefield cannot take further actions during the current battle. However, they can take part in later battles as long as they have at least one point of life remaining.

- Death -
  Units that have no remaining life are deceased. Death is not reversible, so they will no longer be able to fight at your side. You can either Dismiss a deceased unit or Scavenge Skills to remove it from your party.

The movement range and elevation difference each unit can traverse vary depending on the movement type of its class. The skills assigned to a unit can also affect movement.
  The Move command can be reset and issued again up until the point another command is issued. This can be useful when you need to reposition a unit to be in range to attack.

- Crossing Gaps -
  Units can leap across gaps a single tile wide, but the other side of the gap must be of equal or lower elevation.

- Elevation Differences -
  The height a unit can jump up or down varies depending on its movement type. This can lead to situations where a unit can jump down to a lower spot but cannot climb back up, forcing a longer return route to be taken.

The predicted outcome of an action is displayed when the cursor is placed on a target. For actions that cause damage, the expected damage dealt is shown on the left, and the chance of success is shown on the right. Check these values before executing a command to take the most effective course of action.

MP (Magic Points) are required to cast spells, and TP (Tactical Points) are required to use skills and finishing moves. MP and TP are reset to 0 at the beginning of each battle, meaning a unit must wait before using abilities that require MP or TP.

- Gaining MP -
  MP are accumulated gradually with the passing of RT.

- Gaining TP -
  TP are accumulated both with the passing of RT, and when a unit attacks or is attacked.

  More powerful actions consume large amounts of MP and TP, so their use must be timed carefully.

Magic-using classes such as Wizards must first make the following preparations to use spells:

- Learning Spells -
  To learn a spell you must first obtain the corresponding arcana. When you have an arcana in your possession, the spell contained within can be learned by selecting Magic under the Party command. Spells can also be learned by using arcana as items during battle.

- Command Skills -
  To use a spell you have learned, you must also learn the command skill for the spell's elemental school. Once a command skill has been learned, it must be assigned before it can be used in battle. After a skill is assigned, it will appear under the Act command.

Example: Casting Heal
1. Obtain the Grimoire Vitalite.

2. Select Learn under Magic from the Party screen, and then select Grimoire Vitalite. The unit will learn the Heal spell.

3. Select Learn under Skills from the Party screen, and learn the Divine Magic command skill.

4. Select Assign under Skills from the Party screen, and assign the Divine Magic command skill.

Consumables such as mend leaf and magic leaf can be used with the Inventory command. All units use consumables from the party's shared inventory.

- Potent Consumables -
  The Field Alchemy support skill is required to use more potent consumables. There are four levels of Field Alchemy, with higher levels granting mastery over a wider range of consumables. You can view the skills required for each from the Inventory command from the Party screen.

Some of the more common debuffs include petrify, poison, stun, sleep, and charm.

- Petrify -
  Petrified units are turned to stone, leaving them powerless to act. Weapon attacks against them will always hit, but the damage done will be greatly reduced. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Poison -
  Poisoned units will take damage for a set number of turns. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain amount of RT has passed.

- Stun -
  Stunned units have a certain chance of losing the ability to act. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Sleep -
  Sleeping units remain stationary and their avoidance of weapon-based attacks is reduced to 0%. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

- Charm -
  Charmed units are temporarily confused and attack their allies. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

  There are many other debuffs besides those listed here. When a unit is affected by a debuff, you can view details about it using the Condition command.

Attacks using weapons or magic are influenced by attack type, element, and race, and each piece of armor has corresponding resistances to these. If a unit is wearing armor highly resistant to a certain attack, the damage taken is reduced.

- Attack Types -
  The three attack types are CRUSHING, PIERCING, and SLASHING, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Elements -
  The eight elements are AIR, EARTH, LIGHTNING, WATER, FIRE, ICE, LIGHT, and DARK, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Races -
  The nine races are HUMAN, BEAST, REPTILE, DRAGON, DIVINE, UMBRA, FAERIE, PHANTOM, and GOLEM. Some races are more or less resistant to certain spells and weapons.

Terrain information for the selected tile is displayed on the battlefield.
  The left value indicates the melee accuracy modifier and the right value the ranged accuracy modifier. Attacking from a position with high values for the attack type used increases the chance of hitting.
  Some classes such as the Octopus receive greater bonuses on certain terrain than other classes.

Experience points and skill points are calculated for the entire battle party and then distributed according to a number of rules.

- Experience Points -
  The experience point total is made up of the base value for the battle and the points added when enemy units are defeated. This number is then distributed based on the classes of the surviving party members. Classes with the greatest number of surviving units receive more experience points.

- Skill Points -
  Skill points are acquired through the actions taken by your units during battle, and then added to the battle party's skill point pool. The points in the pool are distributed evenly among surviving units once the battle is over.

- Zombies -
  Be wary if any of your surviving units are zombies. Units with this condition count towards the total for point distribution, but receive no actual experience or skill points, so their portion of the total is lost.

Class levels are managed by party rather than by individual units. For example, when you reach level 7 in the Warrior class, all Warrior units in your party will become level 7. This applies to newly recruited units as well, meaning even a new recruit can immediately become a level 7 Warrior in this example.

Each unit can equip up to 5 items. However, items can only be equipped to certain location slots.

- Left Hand/Right Hand -
  Weapons and shields are equipped to hand slots. Two one-handed weapons can be equipped at the same time, but only one two-handed weapon can be equipped. Shields can only be equipped in the left hand.
  
- Armor -
  Two pieces of armor can be equipped, covering head, body, arms, or legs.

- Jewelry -
  A single piece of jewelry can be equipped.

Using the Party command you can view information about each unit in your party and customize their equipment and skills.
  Select a unit from the list and press the {icon 3} button to move to the unit information screen. Here you can perform actions such as changing a unit's equipment or class.
  Press the {icon 4} button while the Unit List is displayed to switch to class list display. This makes it easy to view details such as the level of each class.

Skills are abilities that each unit can learn by spending the skill points they acquire. Each class has access to different skills, but some can be used by other classes once they have been learned. You can increase the number of skill slots by spending skill points, up to a maximum of 10 slots.

  The four skill types are command, support, action, and special.

- Command Skills -
  These add sub-commands that can be accessed using the Act command. Includes skills such as Divine Magic.

- Support Skills -
  Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned. There are many kinds, such as those that change movement type or increase attack power.

- Action Skills -
  Action skills can be executed using the Skills command once they are assigned. They require TP to use.

- Special Skills -
  These include skills such as dragon breath that are only available to certain races. They appear under the Act command.

  Units can gain proficiency with certain skills when they are used in battle, raising their skill rank. You may even acquire finishing moves unique to certain weapons by raising the skill rank of your weapon skills.

The Warren Report contains details of past events, profiles of the people you've met, and news from throughout the isles.

- Recommended Viewing -
  Some events can only be seen from the report. In fact, reading the report may sometimes reveal new locations on the world map. Be sure to peruse it whenever you have the chance.

- Events Past and Present -
  Talk and People contain information about current happenings in Valeria, while the Wheel of Fortune, Tidings, and Play Guide detail the history you've helped to write. Keep this in mind when viewing each category.

You may be drawn into battle at locations on the world map you've visited before. These are known as optional battles.
  During optional battles you may face unique enemies and monsters that are seldom seen elsewhere. They're also a chance to obtain rare items. What's more, {hero} does not need to take part in optional battles, and you can even choose to retreat from them entirely.

- Two Forms of Retreat -
  You can retreat either while forming a battle party before battle, or after battle commences. If you retreat before entering battle, it does not count towards your battles fought. You can see how many battles you've fought in the Warren Report.

You can craft items in shops to upgrade your current equipment and create new pieces not normally offered for sale.
  Crafting requires a recipe and the necessary ingredients and items. There is a risk that crafting may fail.

Your party can contain up to 50 units. You cannot recruit new units after the maximum has been reached; you must first dismiss one or more units to make room. The guests that join you as you make your way through the story do not count toward your unit total.

The skills of a unit with no remaining life can be transferred to another unit. This is called scavenging skills. The Scavenge Skills command is only available when a deceased unit is selected on the party screen.
  A silver oberyth is needed to scavenge skills. Upon selecting a recipient, all skills learned by the deceased unit will be transferred. You cannot scavenge skills from a unit that has not learned any skills. These units can only be dismissed.

The accuracy of attacks is affected by the facing of the target. Attacks from the side are more accurate than those from the front, and attacks from the rear are more accurate than those from the side.
  When targeted by an attack, you have better avoidance from the side than from the rear, and better avoidance from the front than from the side. Prepare for potential enemy attacks by choosing your facing wisely at the end of each turn.

Units can use melee weapons such as swords and axes to attack enemies at higher or lower positions. Weapons with a range of 1 can reach enemies at elevations up to 2 higher and 3 lower than the attacking unit. Floating units can reach elevations 3 higher and lower.

Ranged weapons are classified as bow-type or crossbow-type depending on their firing arc.

- Bow-Type Weapons -
  Bow-type weapons fire projectiles in an arc. Thrown stones are included in this category.

- Crossbow-Type Weapons -
  Crossbow-type weapons fire projectiles in a straight line. Ninja throwing blades are included in this category.

  When making a ranged attack from high ground, you can target units outside the normal weapon range. Conversely, when making a ranged attack from low ground, even targets within range can be difficult to hit.

Weapon skill ranks can be raised by assigning a weapon skill and attacking with the corresponding weapon. Once the skill rank is high enough, the unit can learn finishing moves unique to that type of weapon.
  Finishing moves require TP to use. They can only be used when the corresponding weapon is equipped. You can view the finishing moves a unit has learned from the Party Menu and during battle.
  Each weapon type has several finishing moves. Higher weapon skill ranks allow access to more powerful finishing moves.

Sometimes an attack causes the target to be moved back one tile. This is called knockback. Knockbacks can occur due to critical hits, as well as skills and specific weapon attacks.
  There are certain situations in which knockback is impossible. In general, knockback moves the target back one tile, but this does not occur if the tile in question contains an obstacle or another unit, or if it is at a higher elevation than the starting tile.

- Causing Knockback -
  It is difficult to make critical hits consistently. Attacking with a shield is a more reliable method. Shields usually have a higher chance of causing knockback. There are also skills that raise the chance of successfully knocking a target back.

- Using Knockback -
  If an enemy is knocked down from a certain height, it will take additional damage from the fall. The damage increases with elevation and the weight of the unit.
  Knocking enemies into chasms or off walls can also cause that unit to lose a life and be removed from the battlefield. However, flying units are not affected by this.

Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned.

- Rampart Aura -
  This skill limits the movement of enemy units. A yellow line encircles tiles surrounding units with this skill assigned. Walking units entering this area are forced to stop regardless of whether they have movement left.

- Counterattack -
  This skill triggers a counterattack following an attack by an enemy unit. Units with this skill assigned will counterattack when targeted by a melee attack as long as their equipped weapon has the necessary range.

  There are many other support skills, such as those that change movement type or increase attack. Choose skills that complement a unit's class and the layout of the battlefield.

Weather can affect the accuracy of attacks and the cost of movement on the battlefield. The worse the weather, the lower attack accuracy will be. The cost of moving through difficult terrain such as swamps also increases in rainy or snowy weather. This penalty further increases with heavy rain or snow.

Press the {icon 12} button during battle to open the System Menu and view information about the battlefield.

- Weather -
  Weather changes between five levels over time. When the weather worsens, it may rain or snow depending on the battlefield.

- Element -
  Each battlefield has an elemental affinity that can be altered by spells and skills. The battlefield's element affects the strength of spells and skills. 

- Condition -
  This indicates any special condition affecting the battlefield. The condition of the battlefield can be altered by skills.

You may discover hidden items when your units move to certain parts of the battlefield. These items are called buried treasure.
  Buried treasure can be found in a wide variety of locations, and sometimes requires that grass or snow be burned away to reveal the earth beneath before it can be discovered.

You can only hold up to 99 of each item. If you obtain more of an item you already carry the maximum of during battle, the excess will be converted to goth. Note that you'll receive less than you would if you had sold the items in a shop.

You can sometimes befriend enemy units by using skills such as Recruit, Coax, and Subdue during battle. The chance of success is affected by range, loyalty, and HP.

- Range -
  You should try to get as close as possible to units you want to recruit. They will often ignore you if you merely shout at them from afar.

- Loyalty -
  Check the loyalty of the enemy unit. Units with lower loyalty are easier to recruit. You can judge the loyalty of a unit from the select help text when its name is selected.

- HP -
  Try to reduce the HP of the enemy unit as much as possible to increase your chances of success. One tenth their maximum HP is a good target.

- Failed Recruitment -
  Each time you fail at recruiting, the target's loyalty increases, making the next attempt more difficult. Try to make the first time count.

Sometimes defeated enemies will leave behind a bag of loot or tarot card.
  Tarot cards can be collected by ending a unit's turn on the tile containing the tarot card. The unit's stats will increase, with different cards affecting different stats.
  Bags of loot are collected in the same way. If a pouch contains an arcana, you can also learn the spell it contains after picking it up.

When battle ends, you will receive experience points, skill points, and the spoils of war. Units may also join or leave your party.

- Collecting Items -
  Bags of loot remaining on the battlefield are collected and the items inside added to your inventory. However, tarot cards are not recovered.

- Units Joining the Party -
  Enemy units you successfully recruit can be added to your party after the battle is over. If you already have the maximum number of units, you must either turn the new unit away or dismiss another unit first.

- Units Leaving the Party -
  If the loyalty of your units falls too low, they will leave after the battle is over. Take note if any of your units voice complaints at the end of a fight.

Units have loyalty to their respective leaders. Though this value is not listed as a stat, it can be guessed from the select help message that appears when their name is selected.
  Units with low loyalty may leave your party at the end of a battle. The loyalty of a unit drops when you take actions they do not support, such as defeating enemies of their own clan.
  Take note if any of your units voice complaints at the end of a fight.

You can set your units to AI control to have them act for themselves during battle. There are six AI settings available, including Melee, which sets a unit to fight aggressively, and Vanguard, which sets a unit to hold the front line.
  When you want to restore manual control, select Manual from the AI menu. When the attack turns of AI units run consecutively, you can interrupt their actions and issue commands by pressing the {icon 4} button.

Your units can step on other monster units in your party during battle. All monster units have an elevation of 3. You can use this to your advantage by bridging a gap 3 steps high and 2 tiles wide by positioning a monster unit below.

Skeletons, ghosts, and zombie units are stilled when their HP reaches 0. Stilled units appear identical to incapacitated units, but when the number above their head reaches 0, they reanimate and rejoin the battle.
  Undead can be hard to defeat, but certain spells and skills can destroy them while in this weakened state.

Some obstacles on the battlefield can be destroyed. When these obstacles are selected, they display an HP value like enemy units. There is not always a need to destroy them, but it can serve to give you a tactical advantage at times.

After fleeing from a skirmish with the Resistance at Hagia Banhamuba, Sherri ended up alone in an abandoned house in Balmamusa. {hero} and Olivya encountered her there by chance when seeking shelter from the rain.

The pirates said to be holed up in Qadriga Fortress were actually remnants of the Liberation Front, thought to have been wiped out at Boed Fortress. Though now few in number, they continued their work under the guise of pirates. Cerya and her comrades agreed to join the Resistance.

{hero} rescued Fusilier Lindl, who had been attacked by the Dark Knight Martym in Grimsby. An expert with firearms, Lindl asked to join the Resistance seeking protection and vengeance against the Dark Knights.
Diego, an old sailor who went to {hero}'s aid during a battle with a band of pirates, lectured him for his short-sightedness about the impact of war.

Catiua's death came just ahead of the final battle with the Bakram. As {hero} mourned his loss, he received word that a small group of Resistance forces had been wiped out by Bakram soldiers.

Believing the sage's prophecy, Canopus, Sir Mirdyn, and Sir Gildas were set to make their way to the Palace of the Dead on Exeter in search of Warren. As soon as he heard of their plans, {hero} offered to accompany them.
As {hero} moved deeper into the Palace of the Dead, a mysterious boy appeared before him. The boy mentioned he sought the king there, before vanishing.

Klaire confided that the Holy Knight Lanselot had saved her life in the battle at Rhime, and regretted being unable to thank him at the time. {hero} also lamented being powerless to prevent what had taken place there.

{hero}, Catiua, and Vyce finally found time to gather at the church in Golyat once more. They reminisced over childhood memories, and discussed how their lives had changed since the sacking of Golyat.

On the first of Godscale, the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom celebrated the second anniversary of its founding. Festivities were held across Heim to mark the occasion. Regent Brantyn Morne announced plans to mend damage done to the Hanging Gardens in the war.

A great tragedy has taken place during Bakram-Valerian Kingdom foundation day celebrations. A procession of the Dark Knights Loslorien has met ambush.
  No Dark Knights were harmed, but a number of onlookers were caught in the conflict. Five were killed, and another twenty-one injured. It is not known who instigated the attack.

The Kingdom of Galgastan has announced Duke Ronwey is to be executed in the coming days. The former leader of the Walister Resistance has been held at Almorica Castle since his defeat several months past.

It has come to light that the knights seen recently in the vicinity of Golyat hail from the Kingdom of New Xenobia to the east. Some fear they may be scouts for a coming invasion, though they deny any such charge. They have taken up with a band of rebels, and a close eye will be kept on their conduct.

Remnants of the Walister Resistance have recaptured Almorica Castle from Galgastani forces. Duke Ronwey was freed, and the Galgastani have been forced to withdraw from the region. Both camps will be watched with great interest.

Almorica Castle was recently recaptured by Resistance partisans, who defeated the occupying Galgastani forces.
  None of the partisans were more than a score in years. Their leader, Pavel, is now celebrated as a hero by the Walister people.

The town of Krysaro near Almorica's border is now under Walister Resistance control. Before their coming Krysaro had become a ghost town strewn with corpses, but residents are now beginning to return.
  Krysaro has long been a center of worship for followers of Vasque, and it is but a matter of time before it returns to its former glory.

Opponents of the Galgastani regime in Coritanae held a large rally upon hearing that Almorica Castle had fallen.
  Many have been secretly critical of Hierophant Balbatos, and now this discontent has come to the fore. The Hierophant is responding with force, slaying all those who speak out against him.

Partisans thought to be behind the attack of a procession in Heim on the first of Godscale have now been apprehended. They are believed to be members of the Liberation Front, a group of Bakram militants loyal to the late King Dorgalua. We now await further announcements.

Nybeth Obdilord, a well-known practitioner of the art of necromancy and the Galgastani consul to Almorica, has gone missing.
  He has not been heard from since the fall of Almorica Castle, and is likely a prisoner of the Walister Resistance. There is grave fear for his safety.

The Liberation Front is made up of Bakram partisans loyal to the late King Dorgalua. Though they promote equality regardless of ethnicity or religious beliefs, their violent tactics have been called into question following a number of civilian deaths.
  Front leader Cerya Phoraena vehemently denies any part in these killings. She states this is merely propaganda targeted at discrediting their cause.

A group of Resistance forces have broken through Galgastani lines at Rhime. Sir Leonar of the Knights of Almorica is thought to be among them.
  Leonar is a senior member of the Resistance, and it is rumored he was sent as envoy to seek aid from the Bakram.

Duke Ronwey has decreed that the Phorampa Wildwood, which has long been neglected due to the war, is to be opened to hunters. Though hunting will first be limited to the southern tracts bordering Tynemouth, other areas are to follow.
  The Walister are growing in power, but they yet lack funds. It is thought they seek to profit from Phorampa's bountiful reserves.

A massacre has taken place at Balmamusa. There are no survivors. Balmamusa was set aside for the Walister by the Kingdom of Galgastani, and all those who perished were of Walister blood. Women and children were spared no mercy as the town was engulfed in flames.
  The killings are thought to be an act of retribution by the Galgastani for the recapture of Almorica Castle by the Resistance. Hierophant Balbatos maintains he is not responsible.

Hearing of the massacre at Balmamusa, factions within the Galgastani camp have risen up against their leaders. They sought to oust the Hierophant, but army forces have crushed the rebellion with a savage display of force. Many are deserting the army or seeking to incite a coup d'état, and the chain of command is in tatters.

The Walister Resistance has placed a bounty on the head of the young Hero of Golyat who recaptured Almorica Castle. They have named him as the one responsible for the massacre at Balmamusa. He has thus far evaded pursuit, and is now in hiding. The bounty stands at a staggering 30,000 goth.

Reports indicate that forces of the Walister Resistance led by Duke Ronwey are massing in the Psonji Weald near Coritanae Keep. Galgastani now make up about half the Resistance army, and the battle lines are no longer as clearly drawn as in the past. It seems a final push will be made in the coming days.

The Walister Resistance has captured Coritanae Keep, the Galgastani seat of power. The keep was taken with little resistance, making the battle of the Psonji Weald the last major engagement of the war. Galgastani leader Hierophant Balbatos was executed the following morning.

Bakram forces launched a new offensive on Rhime mere days after the downfall of the Kingdom of Galgastan. They now battle soldiers of the Walister Resistance garrisoned there, and both sides have suffered heavy losses. Refugees from Rhime are streaming into the Phidoch region.

Another tragedy reminiscent of the massacre at Balmamusa has occurred. A great many of the townspeople of Rhime have fallen victim to the Bakram invasion. At least 5,000 are believed dead, and bodies litter the streets. With skirmishes still taking place, as yet nothing can be done to put the dead to rest.

Meanwhile, opponents of the Hierophant in Galgastan are still wary of laying the blame for the massacre on Balbatos.

Reports indicate that the Galgastani forces led by Hierophant Balbatos are massing in the Psonji Weald near Coritanae Keep. With the Resistance growing in numbers and Galgastani opponents of the war becoming more vocal, it is thought Galgastani forces will make their move soon.

Curious posters have been sighted in Rhime in recent days. They say simply, "The nobility must be overthrown." They are the work of the New Walister Alliance, who seek self-governance for their people. Support for this new faction is growing fast among the poorer classes, and authorities seek to unmask its leader.

A major battle has been fought between Galgastani and Walister forces at the Psonji Weald. Both sides incurred heavy losses in fighting that raged for more than a day, but the Galgastani emerged victorious. The Resistance were unfamiliar with the lay of the land, and the Galgastani clinched victory upon the arrival of reinforcements.

Ravness Loxaerion, sought by the Resistance for her involvement in the massacre at Balmamusa, has been captured at Port Asyton in the Kingdom of Galgastan.
  She led Resistance forces in a number of past battles, and is a bitter enemy of Galgastan. The Resistance requested she be handed over to them, but the Galgastani camp refused. She is to be escorted to Coritanae Keep where she faces execution.

Duke Ronwey of the Walister Resistance has met with Galgastani leaders to negotiate the dissolution of the army and the formal handover of Coritanae. This signals the end of the Kingdom of Galgastan established by Hierophant Balbatos.

Former Galgastani soldiers are flocking to the Walister Resistance. Many of them long to end the war that has stretched on for more than two years, and they are eager to prove their mettle against the Bakram armies.

A large number of refugees fled Rhime for neighboring regions when the Bakram invaded. Those who had taken up in Phidoch have started to make their way home. The Bakram claim the restoral of public order in Rhime is to thank for this, but refugees state their poor treatment at the hands of the people of Phidoch has forced them to leave.

Mount Weobry in the Burnham Massif has erupted for the first time in six score years. The blast shook the land for miles, but tremors have now subsided.
  Though the Valerian Isles are volcanic, Mount Hedon on Banhamuba was the only known active volcano until now.

Almorica Castle has been attacked by remnants of the Galgastani army. The Resistance suffered few losses, but were caught off guard by the late-night assault, and the castle fell.
  Elite Galgastani forces were made up of Balbatos loyalists, and most have continued to fight. Though Coritanae has been annexed, it will be some time before the Resistance wins the hearts of its people.

Vyce Bozeck, once a top member of the Resistance, now has a bounty of 50,000 goth on his head. This is the largest in recorded history. Vyce is accused of plotting to kill Duke Ronwey, and has not been seen for over a month. He was the childhood friend of {hero} Pavel, the Hero of Golyat.

The bounty for Vyce Bozeck, wanted for plotting the assassination of Duke Ronwey, now stands at 60,000 goth.

Valeria has a thriving sea trade, and many fortresses have been built to protect its ports from enemies. During King Dorgalua's reign soldiers of the Kingdom of Valeria were garrisoned at each fortress, but since the kingdom's downfall they have been manned sporadically at best. This has led to an increase in pirates, bandits, and army stragglers capturing the fortresses for their own use. Gecho Fortress on Beneceunga fell into pirate hands just the other day.
  As Gecho is south of the prominent trading port of Grimsby, merchants there are anxious to see the pirates routed from the fortress as soon as possible.

Rumor has it that remnants of the Galgastani army are gathering at Lhazan Fortress, site of the recent Bakram massacre of Vasque faithful. The Galgastani soldiers' plans are not known, but they could seek to use the fortress as a stronghold to fight the Resistance.

A large number of refugees fled Rhime for neighboring regions when the Bakram invaded. Those who had taken up in Phidoch have started to make their way home. The Bakram claim the restoral of public order in Rhime is to thank for this, but refugees state their poor treatment at the hands of the people of Phidoch has forced them to leave.

Mount Weobry in the Burnham Massif has erupted for the first time in six score years. The blast shook the land for miles, but tremors have now subsided.
  Though the Valerian Isles are volcanic, Mount Hedon on Banhamuba was the only known active volcano until now.

Duke Ronwey was slain at Almorica Castle while Resistance and Bakram forces battled at Rhime. A close ally, Sir Leonar, was behind the killing. Since the massacre at Balmamusa there had been growing concern about the Duke's ability to lead, and this ultimately led to his demise.

A new leader of the Walister Resistance has emerged following the Duke's death. The Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel, who acted swiftly to put down Leonar's rebellion, now heads the Resistance. {hero} has also allied with the New Walister Alliance, which enjoys a great deal of support among the people.

Reports indicate that the Galgastani forces led by Hierophant Balbatos are massing in the Psonji Weald south of Coritanae Keep. They are likely to strike while the Resistance is preoccupied with the Bakram invasion of Rhime and the change of leadership following Sir Leonar's assassination of the Duke.

The Galgastani seat of power, Coritanae Keep, has fallen. It seems Resistance soldiers battling the Galgastani at the Psonji Weald were merely decoys, as another force led by the Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel, assailed the undermanned keep. Galgastani leader Hierophant Balbatos was killed in the fighting.

Many Galgastani soldiers surrendered to the Walister Resistance following the death of Hierophant Balbatos. The Resistance took control of major cities such as Port Asyton and the mining town of Balmamusa. As the Galgastani forces sent to the Psonji Weald remain at large, surrendering soldiers are held as prisoners of war to prevent them joining the fray again.

The Resistance stronghold Almorica Castle has fallen to Galgastani stragglers. The assault was led by High Commander Xaebos, a close aid of the late Hierophant Balbatos. He played a key role in the blood war, and is wanted for crimes committed against the peoples of Valeria. He has also taken Resistance officer Vyce Bozeck prisoner.

Former Galgastani soldiers are flocking to the Walister Resistance. Many of them long to end the war that has stretched on for more than two years, and they are eager to prove their mettle against the Bakram armies.

Almorica Castle has been liberated by Resistance forces. High Commander Xaebos was slain in the battle. The Galgastani stragglers who had continued fighting the Resistance are now no more. This signals the end of the Kingdom of Galgastan established by the late Hierophant Balbatos.

The Lord of Coritanae, premier of the Kingdom of Galgastan, has gone missing. Hierophant Balbatos has declared the Lord kidnapped by those seeking to exploit his position. The search is ongoing.
  No strangers were sighted in the vicinity of the Lord's quarters, nor have any traces of an intruder been found, so authorities believe it the work of an insider. Denizens of the keep fear greatly for their Lord's safety, and worry at reports of the Resistance's advance.
