Having the backing of both Resistance leaders and the commons, Princess Versalia announced her intention to establish Heim as the provisional seat for her throne. Many of the Princess's closest allies are to aid in her rule.
  She has also announced the Resistance is to be dissolved. With war at an end and the Dark Knights destroyed, the Resistance has already fulfilled its purpose. Its soldiers will join the Queen's guard or be assigned other posts to ensure they are rewarded for the service they have given.
  Heim Castle is bustling with the preparations for Versalia's coronation.

With the Heim Conflict that erupted following the death of King Dorgalua at an end, King Tristan of the Kingdom of New Xenobia pledged to support Princess Versalia in restoring the isles to their former glory. It is rumored that his envoys have already been sent to Heim.
  The Holy Lodissian Empire has made no comment thus far. With the collapse of the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom they had lent aid to through a secret treaty, they surely cannot remain silent for much longer. Interestingly, it seems the destruction of the Dark Knights has yet to be announced in Lodis.

Though the war in Valeria is at an end, bands of armed militia still roam the lands. The Tigers of Burnham is one such group. Based in the Burnham Highlands, they have been implicated in a number of assassinations.
  They recently claimed that {hero} Pavel, leader of the Resistance, is using Princess Versalia to gain power for himself. They have stated their intention to capture Heim from the Resistance and restore rightful order under Versalia's rule.
  Though they fight under the banner of justice for all Valerians, former Bakram and Galgastani soldiers are joining their ranks in droves, and doubts have been cast on their motives.

The Bay of Gobanda is known for the thick fog that hangs over its waters. It was recently discovered that an immense tower lies hidden within the fog.
  Scholars from the Royal Academy say it once stood in the ancient city of San Bronsa, which was destroyed in Dorgalua's great war. The Bay of Gobanda was formed when magic wielded by King Rodrick of Brigantys shattered the lands in the last days of the war, also destroying San Bronsa.
  Scholars had studied the tower before the great war, but it is still not known when it was built, or by whom. It is said the Hanging Gardens built by King Dorgalua were inspired by the tower of San Bronsa.
  As news of the tower's discovery spreads there is concern it will be looted by thieves, and the Resistance is considering sending an exploratory party there. There have been further reports of a large island floating in the sky above the bay, but nothing more is known at this point.

Many strange rumors have been circulating of late. People thought dead have been seen walking about, and the same person sighted in two places at once. Normally little stock would be put into such rumors, but there is much talk about these incidents among scholars and mages. Some believe them the work of the Apocrypha, others attribute them to some arcane art brought from Lodis.
  A common thread is found throughout these reports. The young hero of the Resistance, {hero}, is always mentioned by witnesses.
  {hero} is famed as a warrior and tactician, but few know of his penchant for collecting tarot cards. He is apparently particularly fond of the Wheel of Fortune card. It is not clear how this relates to the current rumors, but the Wheel of Fortune card has long been a symbol of regret and atonement in Valeria. It would not be beyond reason for {hero} himself to be struggling with such feelings, having experienced war at such a young age.
  What would one do if the power to bend time fell into our hands? One could repeat an exercise, knowing the best solution in advance. Or learn a lover plans to leave you before they speak a word. And who would not go back to save the lives of fallen comrades?
  However, one thing must be kept in mind: A different past is no guarantee of a happier future. Changing what has happened may in fact have no effect at all on the here and the now.

The songstress Iuria has won great fame for her talents, but since her arrival death seems to stalk the sick and weak in Omish. The requiems she sings when the dead are laid to rest may bring tears with their beauty, but some believe her to be the dreaded Wicce Sirene.

A stone tablet found at the Palace of the Dead on Exeter this month past has been deciphered. Scholars at the Royal Academy announced the tablet to contain the message, "A sealed door lies three floors below ground." This discovery already appears to be common knowledge among treasure-hunting thieves.

In the ancient Bolsenian era, the Dragon Lords built a civilization that flourished across Xytegenia and the surrounding isles. They are said to be the source of the magic practiced today, but much of this knowledge perished with them. On rare occasions arcana from this era are discovered at ancient ruins, and these are highly sought after.

A ceremony celebrating Princess Versalia's return to power was held at Heim Castle. Bakram officials who served King Dorgalua, including Regent Brantyn Morne, pledged their allegiance to the Princess. Lord Tartaros also attended as representative of High Priest Sardian of the Holy Lodissian Empire, reaffirming the alliance between the two nations.

{order}, which incorporates soldiers of the former Walister Resistance and the armies of Galgastan, appears to be faltering.
  Still known as the Resistance, they pledge to fight the Bakram, but following the capture of Phidoch Castle a stalemate has been reached, and some of their number now believe the war to be futile. We will keep a close watch on further developments.

The Order of Philaha was divided by infighting following the death of King Dorgalua, with current leader Regent Morne ousting Archiereus Mreuva. However, Mreuva has gained many supporters since his removal, and a great number of followers wish him reinstated when Princess Versalia returns to power.

Archiereus Mreuva was leader of the Order of Philaha during the rule of King Dorgalua. He was ousted by Regent Morne, who was Exarch at the time, and fled Heim to continue his work alone. It has recently come to light that Mreuva has joined forces with the Resistance. Mreuva is immensely popular, and will serve as a strong ally to the Resistance.

Resistance forces are advancing on Heim. A large Bakram contingent has also been seen leaving the capital. However, no Dark Knights accompany the Bakram, lending weight to rumors of a falling out between them. The armies will soon clash head to head.

A mysterious blast has been heard on Exeter, an island northwest of the Valerian mainland. Exeter is the site of the dungeon known as the Palace of the Dead. Many have entered its halls seeking riches, but the few who have returned did so empty handed. Some believe the blast to be magical in nature.

In times long past, mankind was engaged in a bitter battle with the forces of evil for supremacy over the land. Man drew strength from their gods, while the forces of evil suckled at the power of the Abyss. In the end, the people could do nothing against the overwhelming might of evil, and were pushed to the brink of destruction.
  It was at this time a group of three knights and twelve sages descended from the heavens and sealed the Chaos Gate that linked our world with the Abyss. The tide was turned, and man emerged victorious. Thus man came to rule and build the civilizations that stand today.
  The battle won, the three knights returned to the heavens, while the twelve sages remained to spread knowledge among the people. However, a burden yet weighed on their hearts. When the forces of evil fled, they foretold another Ogre Battle would occur. One of the knights bestowed a sword upon man that would grant the power to call the gods once more.
  The sword's name was Brynhildr. It is said he who wields the blade can speak with the gods, and travel to the heavens and the Abyss. The sword became an object of worship, and was hidden away until a second Ogre Battle saw need of its powers.

Upon hearing that Princess Versalia was held captive by the Dark Knights, the Resistance launched an attack on Barnicia Castle. Though the castle was captured, the Princess was slain by the Dark Knights before she could be rescued. The Dark Knights face outrage for their reckless actions. Loslorien themselves deny the allegations.

Upon hearing that Princess Versalia was held captive by the Dark Knights, the Resistance launched an attack on Barnicia Castle. The castle was captured, and the Princess is now safely back in Resistance hands. The Dark Knights claim the Resistance are holding the Princess as a prisoner of war, but the Princess denies this.

Salvage work has begun on the wreck of the Rhamsen, which sank in a storm off Legat. The Rhamsen was a merchant vessel bound from Balboede to the south. Thankfully the mostly Balboeden crew escaped unharmed, but their precious cargo sank with the ship. The Dark Knights are assisting with the recovery of the lost cargo.

Heim Castle has been captured. Brantyn Morne, ruler of the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom, was slain in the battle for the castle. Bakram soldiers throughout the lands have surrendered together with senior Bakram leaders. This brings an end to the war that has raged since the death of King Dorgalua.

Loslorien and Bakram soldiers yet to yield to the Resistance have taken refuge at the Hanging Gardens. The Hanging Gardens is a tower of eighteen floors built during the reign of King Dorgalua, with lush greenery on each floor fed by ever-flowing fountains.

After the fall of Heim Castle, a curious rumor spread among the captured Dark Knights. They claim a Loslorien knight had infiltrated the Resistance. The Resistance is looking into the matter, as if there is truth to the rumor, it may mean one of their own is working against them.

An enchanting winged songstress has arrived in Port Omish, a town of ruffians and rogues. People flock to hear her angelic voice day upon day.
  It is rare to see winged womenfolk in those parts, and she has become quite a spectacle.

Public order in Valeria is at an all time low due to the lengthy war. It is now commonplace for caravans to be beset by bandits, and pirates attack merchant vessels with abandon. The protection of sea trade is of particular import to Valeria, so a solution must be found soon. Qadriga Fortress is said to be one of many pirate strongholds scattered across Valeria.

There have been a number of raids on caravans near the town of Grimsby on Legat, known as a center for trade. Grimsby has long fended off bandits with the fortifications built across the town, but now raiders are said to attack from the sky. The bandits are believed to be camped in the Neimrahava Wood outside town.

Law and order has suffered due to the lengthy war, but one town has been a haven for lawlessness since the rule of King Dorgalua. Southwest of Qadriga Fortress lies Ubeia, site of the outlaw's haven called Omish.
  Omish has a long history as a stopover port for sea traders, but over time it became a haunt for pirates, and it now operates under its own laws. It is also home to many criminals and former soldiers seeking anonymity, as well as refugees who lost their homes in Dorgalua's great war.

On the island of Oedlark off the southernmost tip of Valeria are a series of undersea caverns known as the Pirate's Graveyard. They are legendary among treasure hunters, said to hold untold riches in their depths.
  The caverns are known for one other thing: countless pirates and thieves have sought to claim the treasures of the cavern as their own, but most lose their lives before even setting foot inside.
  Currents from the south and northwest converge in the waters surrounding the Pirate's Graveyard, and its reefs make navigation difficult for all but the most skilled sailors.
  Upon reaching the caverns explorers must contend with all manner of deadly creatures, and it is littered with the corpses of failed adventurers. It is no wonder that none have yet claimed the treasures said to lie within.

Many pirates and treasure hunters have lost their lives at the Pirate's Graveyard. Only one man has returned from its depths alive. The Dread Pirate Azelstan is known throughout the Obero Sea.
  Boasting superb navigation skills and uncommon prowess with the sword, he was a pirate among pirates. He was also known for his cruelty, said to have left a trail of blood wherever his ship sailed, and his name struck fear into the hearts of all.
  Soon after returning from the Pirate's Graveyard, Azelstan gave up pirating and disappeared. Many have speculated at why he retired in the years that have passed, some saying he was cursed by a spectre, others claiming his sword arm was maimed at the Pirate's Graveyard.

On the island of Oedlark off the southernmost tip of Valeria are a series of undersea caverns known as the Pirate's Graveyard. They are legendary among treasure hunters, said to hold untold riches in their depths.
  The caverns are known for one other thing: countless pirates and thieves have sought to claim the treasures of the cavern as their own, but most lose their lives before even setting foot inside.
  Currents from the south and northwest converge in the waters surrounding the Pirate's Graveyard, and its reefs make navigation difficult for all but the most skilled sailors.
  Upon reaching the caverns explorers must contend with all manner of deadly creatures, and it is littered with the corpses of failed adventurers. It is no wonder that none have yet claimed the treasures said to lie within.
  To obtain this treasure one would need a guide such as the Dread Pirate Azelstan, who navigated the deadly waters of the Pirate's Graveyard and returned from its depths unscathed.

Six fortresses scattered across Valeria serve to protect it from foreign enemies. But few are aware that these were not built as strongholds. The fortresses were temples dedicated to the six daughters of the Great Father Philaha.
  The temple areas remain today, but the entryways from the fortifications were sealed during the reign of King Dorgalua. No one knows why the temples were sealed off, or how the seals can be broken.

The fifteen years of war before Valeria was unified is known as Dorgalua's great war.
  Before the unification, Valeria was divided into the five kingdoms of Barnicia, Phidoch, Almorica, Coritanae, and Brigantys. Each sought to expand their territory, and relations were volatile to say the least.
  The great war began after Lord Clemont of Barnicia was assassinated by armed militia seeking to usurp his leadership. The delicate balance of power soon crumbled, with Phidoch gathering its military might and declaring war on Barnicia and Almorica, while Coritanae joined the fray as Almorica's ally.
  The war stretched on for eight years, with Phidoch eventually occupying Barnicia and Almorica and installing governments there. Phidoch ruler King Ramonica was a Bakram, and he began suppressing the Walister, causing friction between the peoples that continues to this day. Great numbers of partisans struggled against him.
  Phidoch attacked Coritanae, and when formerly neutral Brigantys joined the war at the behest of Coritanae, the war spread throughout the entire Valerian Isles. Fighting soon reached a stalemate, but Brigantys began secretly supporting partisan groups, who then formed a rebel army in Barnicia.
  Coritanae ruler Count Orlandeau was killed in battle, and Coritanae fell under the rule of Brigantys. The rebel army of Barnicia then turned on Phidoch. Future king Dorgalua was leader of this rebel army. Beset on both flanks by Brigantys and the rebels, Phidoch fell at last, bringing the conflict to an end.   
  King Rodrick of Brigantys agreed to a truce with Dorgalua, but the conditions favored one side greatly, and it was broken within a month. Fighting began anew. The battle between Rodrick and Dorgalua continued for another year, with Dorgalua ultimately winning victory. Valeria was united under a single ruler at last.

Towards the end of Dorgalua's great war, King Rodrick of Brigantys wielded terrible magic to break the deadlocked armies. The great power this unleashed defeated his enemies on the battlefield en masse, but slew his allies in kind. The surrounding lands were also shattered beyond recognition.
  Upon his victory over King Rodrick, King Dorgalua forbade the use of the Apocrypha, and hid them away. Knowledge of its very existence was lost to the sands of time.

There have been rumors of discord between the Bakram and Dark Knights, and now it seems there is internal strife in the Dark Knights as well. A Bakram soldier revealed he saw Dark Knight commanders quarreling in Barnicia Castle.
  The details of the dispute are not known, but over the past weeks the Dark Knights have been linked to dishonorable acts such as the massacre at Rhime and the fall of Phidoch Castle. The Dark Knights may be looking for a scapegoat on which to lay the blame, but thus far they have remained silent on the matter.

In recent memory Balmamusa has been the site of a tragic massacre, and now it bears witness to a tragedy of a different kind. Legions of walking dead now stalk the town, having appeared out of nowhere.
  It is not known where they originated. We can but hope they will be stopped before too much damage is done.

The songstress Iuria has been the talk of the town of late, and new information about her has come to light. It seems she travels to the deadly caverns known as the Pirate's Graveyard night after night. These caverns are surrounded by treacherous waters, and are said to be a gathering place for souls of the dead.
  This suspicious behavior lends more weight to rumors that Iuria is in fact the Wicce Sirene.

It is not commonly known that the Brigania Flats were once a lush paradise. The Bay of Gobanda was also once an inland area.
  In the final days of Dorgalua's great war, the lands were shattered by a man named Rodrick Desmoria, who was once King of Brigantys.
  He fought alongside King Dorgalua to unite Valeria, but in the end became his mortal enemy. He is known for using forbidden magic to wipe out those who opposed him. Though his reputation is marred by this, King Rodrick was an austere ruler who would not stand for injustice or compromise. He at first resolved to use the Apocrypha to aid his people, but it was this act that caused them to turn against him.
  It is said he died in captivity at Brigantys Castle after his defeat at the hands of King Dorgalua. Until his death he muttered constantly of the injustice he had suffered, and some say his spirit was called to the Palace of the Dead after his passing.

The war is at an end, and peace has returned to Valeria. Reconstruction work is moving at a swift pace across the lands, and although trade has not reached its previous levels, it recovers day by day. The markets once again throng with people, and fresh vegetables and fruit from far away countries line the stalls. The lively seafaring country of Valeria is back to its old self.
  Yet many still bear the wounds of war. Veterans of the fighting are left scarred, dealing with lost limbs, blindness, and paralysis.
  Princess Versalia has ordered these soldiers be granted a benefit through the Order of Philaha. This may cost up to a quarter of the kingdom's budget, and could climb to almost half if compensation for civilians is also approved.
  Those dealing with postwar matters such as these are at a loss to help those suffering trauma from the horrors they faced in the war. In many cases this trauma affects the everyday lives of victims, causing insomnia and anxiety, and it can only be alleviated through medicinal means. Sufferers sometimes turn to drink as a way of escape, and it is clear this is a problem than cannot be resolved through medical care alone.
  Archiereus Mreuva Phoraena heads a committee dealing with the postwar recovery that pledges support to all, regardless of background, class, or profession. Those seeking help should inquire at the nearest abbey.

The motives behind many of Loslorien's activities have long been a mystery; the attack on Golyat, a town on the island of Galdochae, chief among them. According to a statement made to the Bakram by Dark Knight commander Balxephon V. Rahms, they planned the attack after learning a group of rebels conducting raids on Heim was hiding there. However, this information was later revealed to be false, and Lodis paid reparation to Golyat for the damage done during the attack.
  Now their true intentions have been revealed. Loslorien conducted the raid without Bakram help, and not one but several commanders were present. The Dark Knight Balxephon was among them, and some witnesses say they saw High Champion Tartaros as well. Even if armed militia were taking refuge there, it is questionable that so many Loslorien elite would take part.
  Despite the many victims of the tragedy at Golyat, there was no record of rebels being captured. Though attempts were made to obtain such records after the war, documents listing the names of suspected rebels were never uncovered. This can mean but one thing: the Dark Knights knew from the start that no rebels were harbored there.
  So why would they commit so brutal an act? Loslorien attacked Golyat after learning of the existence of a daughter born to King Dorgalua, most likely through Regent Brantyn Morne. It is also thought they had no intention of forming a long-term alliance with Brantyn and the Bakram. They acted under the pretense of eliminating rebel forces to conceal their true intentions.
  Yet after all their efforts, they were not able to locate the Princess in the attack. Instead, they instilled a hatred of Lodis in the Walister and created the Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel.
  Two years have passed since the raid on Golyat. With the war at an end, and Loslorien now back in Lodis, peace has returned to Valeria. Golyat has recovered swiftly, and few traces of the war remain. It should not be long before Golyat regains its status as Oberon's Pearl.
  In the coming days the unveiling of a monument will take place in the central plaza in Golyat. The monument was constructed at the behest of Princess Versalia to honor the memory of those who died in the attack, and remember how those precious lives brought the people of Valeria together.
  The Valerian Isles are now host to many visitors. We can but hope that those who see this new symbol of Golyat will take home with them a desire for peace.
